correctness.rationale: Complete all-n proof: positive trinomial factors give strictly increasing continuous argument of \(F(\mathrm{i}x)\), implying oriented alternating negative roots of even and odd coefficient polynomials. Their Bernoulli parameters interleave; coupling via independent common uniforms proves two stochastic inequalities. The monotone quantile coupling moves each matched sample by exactly \(\frac12\), meeting the universal lattice-separation lower bound for every Wasserstein order. Positive-parity normalizers allow boundary approximation. The packaged script exhaustively checks 54,240 rational cases with 551,570 exact CDF inequalities and additional rational couplings; these finite tests are supplementary.

originality.rationale: The inspected 2026 primary paper establishes parity-conditioned real-rooted Poisson-binomial laws and mean/mode proximity, not a common optimal nearest-neighbor transport or exact Wasserstein metric. Classical Hurwitz/Hermite–Biehler machinery gives interlacing of polynomial zeros but does not itself state the probabilistic coupling. The proposed result adds two cross-indexed stochastic comparisons and an exact global transport optimum. Historical searches yielded no directly dominating statement. A similar earlier mode-distance statement is not a distributional transport theorem; the common polynomial ingredient is disclosed.

value.rationale: The full-lattice optimal coupling answers a natural comparison question in probabilistic win/tie/loss score sums. It is an exact, sharp invariant simultaneously for all Wasserstein orders and all heterogeneous independent inputs, robust to boundary zeros. It improves the original inter-parity mean bound 1 to the sharp \(\frac12\) and gives uniform control for all Lipschitz score functionals. Modal proximity alone does not furnish such full-law transport. The result has a clear object-level motivation and is not a numerical table or arbitrary slice.
